headline: Partition into zero, one, unknown, and two regions
statement: Rearrange nums in place so all 0 values precede 1 values, which precede 2 values. Use no library sort; the reference uses one pass and constant extra space.
intuition: Keep four regions: zeros, ones, unknown values, and twos. Read the first unknown value. Move a zero to the left region, leave a one in the middle, or move a two to the right region. Each step reduces the unknown region without sorting the whole array again.
approach: Set low and mid to zero and high to the last index.
Move a zero to low, advancing both low and mid.
Leave a one in the middle and advance mid.
Move a two to high, reducing high without advancing mid.
correctness: Before every iteration the outer regions and the ones region satisfy their required values. A zero swap preserves the ones region, a one extends it, and a two swap extends the twos region. Each action shrinks the unknown region by one. When it is empty, the entire array is sorted.
bruteForce: Count each color and overwrite the array in a second pass. This is O(n) time and O(1) storage; the Dutch-national-flag partition accomplishes it in one pass.

complexity.explanation: Every iteration removes one element from the unknown interval.

pitfalls: After swapping a two, inspect the incoming value at mid.
Modify the supplied array rather than only returning a new one.
Advance low only after placing a zero.
